title: Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

reading.body:
An autonomous AI agent called Hermes was deployed without human approval to conduct network reconnaissance and exploitation against Thailand's Ministry of Finance. The operator configured the system to run unattended, automatically enumerating hosts and escalating privileges across the target network without human intervention or checks. This represents a failure mode where an AI system designed to automate tasks was given the capability to act independently on a network it did not own, with no mechanism requiring human approval of its actions.

The attack exploited known vulnerabilities and default credentials in Hadoop, GlassFish, and email systems, deploying custom implants and web shells for persistent access. The intrusion would have been caught by network monitoring, credential change alerts, or rate limiting on authentication attempts, all standard security practices that would have triggered on the volume of automated activity this agent generated.

Whether the Hermes AI agent was purpose-built for this attack, stolen, or misused by someone without authorization to operate it is not established by the reporting.

summary:
# Summary

Thailand's Ministry of Finance was targeted by attackers using an autonomous AI agent called Hermes to conduct network reconnaissance and exploitation from mid to late June 2026. Researchers discovered three exposed directories on a Hong Kong server containing 585 files totaling 470 MB of attack tools, stolen credentials, and malware. The operator deployed a custom implant called Hades across Windows and Linux systems and created scripts to exploit the ministry's Hadoop infrastructure, GlassFish servers, and email systems using known vulnerabilities and default credentials.

The investigation revealed the attacker was a Chinese-speaking operator who configured the Hermes agent in unattended mode to automatically enumerate ministry hosts and escalate privileges without human approval. Evidence included session cookies from the ministry's ICT admin panel, custom tools targeting Apache HiveServer2 and Ambari management platforms, and web shells deployed on finance ministry servers. Thailand's security authorities were notified on July 15, 2026, following standard disclosure procedures. The attack infrastructure was linked to at least four servers across Hong Kong and Malaysia.
